components.name: Task Sheet
components.description: Right-hand slideover for task details; the board behind it dims under a 40% dark neutral scrim (neutral-900/40) so the bright sheet keeps contrast. No close button.

components.name: App Bar
components.description: One pill with the brand and the two places, plus a third segment while on a page behind ⋯ (#583); the selected segment sits on one raised chip that glides between them. ⋯ is never selected. No ink fill. Top on desktop, floating at the bottom on a phone.

narrative.overview:
A tidy desk under a good lamp. One sheet is in front of you, the rest is stacked neatly to the side, and nothing on the desk asks for attention it hasn't earned. Kan-Do is a working tool (Operate mode): the board is scanned many times a day in short glances, so calm comes from restraint, predictability and generous space, not from decoration.

The desk is warm, not austere. Calm comes from generous composition (few things per screen, large confident headings, space between groups), friendly rounded warmth (warm paper neutrals, soft radii, one approachable sans), flows that happen in place (a question asked on the card, a value edited in its row) and small physical motion that explains what just happened. Airbnb is the positive reference for all four. Trello (rainbow labels, gamified clutter) and Notion (dense, technical, information overload) are the anti-references: no dense toolbars, no sidebar overload, no modal on modal.
keyCharacteristics: Warm paper page, bright card sheets, one quiet ink accent.
One typeface; type and space compose the page, not boxes, lines or fills.
Flat by default; soft, ambient shadows only on things you can pick up.
Questions are asked in place; reversible actions act at once and offer undo.
Motion is small and physical and explains a state change.
Light only for now (`colorMode: false`); dark mode would be a new feature, designed from scratch.

rules.name: The One Lamp Rule
rules.body: Ink is the only accent. If more than one element per view is ink-filled, one of them is wrong.

rules.name: The Status Is Not Decoration Rule
rules.body: Teal means done, orange means attention, raspberry means destructive or failed. They never appear for emphasis, branding or variety. Integration brand colours (Todoist red, Notion black) do not appear in the UI; sources are shown in neutral ink. A topic's own hue lives on its mark only (The Topic Mark Rule).

rules.name: The Topic Mark Rule
rules.body: A topic may carry a hue and a symbol on its mark only: a small dot or glyph before the name. The name stays neutral muted text. Never a coloured chip, label, card, stack, column or surface, and never a hue on a name in a list or table. One mark per topic, from the nine `--topic-*` tokens; no mark at all for a topic with neither hue nor symbol. This is the one place where hue encodes the user's own category rather than status (decision D2, #430/#431).

rules.name: The Frozen Primary Rule
rules.body: The primary palette (Ink, hue 255) changes only by a decision recorded here (the user's, or an agent's marked `agent-decided` on its issue), never as a side effect of a feature.

rules.name: The Receding Text Rule
rules.body: Waiting cards, done titles and placeholders step down through a token colour, never through `opacity` on text, and text keeps body contrast. Status text sits on its own wash in the deep step of its colour. A deliberate exception (today: the Jetzt focus overlay dimming the rest of the board, and the muted content of a collapsed stack's front card) is a recorded decision: it is reversible or purely a signal, documented with its component, and exempted narrowly in the a11y test.

rules.name: The One Role Rule
rules.body: `font-display` (Figtree 600) is only for display and headline roles (headings and numerals; never labels, tab names, prompts or plain sentences). Body, labels and card titles stay at 400-500.

rules.name: The Three Line-Heights Rule
rules.body: `--lh-tight` for display text, `--lh-snug` for compact UI, `--lh-body` for reading. No other line-heights.

rules.name: The Only Cards Float Rule
rules.body: Cards carry the custom shadows. The named exceptions are the desktop task sheet (cast toward the board) and modals (a hairline ring plus a soft downward shadow, so a dialog separates by its surface, not by a stronger scrim). Popovers, dropdowns and menus keep Nuxt UI defaults; nothing else gets a shadow. Waiting cards sink through greyscale and a toned title, not through shadow changes.

dos: **Do** follow the styling priority: (1) Nuxt UI semantic tokens (`text-muted`, `bg-elevated`, `text-primary`) → (2) baseline overrides in `assets/css/main.css` → (3) custom domain tokens in `assets/css/main.css`.
**Do** put component overrides in `app.config.ts → ui.<component>` and verify slot names via the Nuxt UI MCP `get-component-metadata` or `.nuxt/ui/<component>.ts`.
**Do** use `bg-page` for the page and board surface, `bg-elevated` for sheets.
**Do** compose pages with type and space: a display heading and a gap before a box, a line or a tint.
**Do** ask small questions in place, and offer undo for anything reversible.
**Do** aim for WCAG 2.2 AA (text 4.5:1, non-text 3:1); `tests/e2e/a11y.spec.ts` checks it.
donts: **Don't** use raw Tailwind palette classes (`text-gray-600`, `bg-red-500`) or arbitrary hex/px values; ESLint warns on them.
**Don't** use ink for more than one filled element per view, or status colours for emphasis.
**Don't** add confirmation dialogs for reversible actions, or a dialog for a question that belongs to one card.
**Don't** nest cards, stack modals, or add toolbars to the board.
**Don't** animate for decoration, loop, or run board transitions during a drag.
**Don't** set body text in the display role (600) or add a second display typeface.
